Colorado’s ONLY dedicated Gluten-Free Farmers Market is back for another incredible season! Hosted by Denver Celiacs, this one-of-a-kind community event was created to provide a safe, welcoming, and inclusive shopping experience for individuals living with celiac disease, gluten intolerance, and gluten-related disorders.

Held monthly from June through October in Englewood, Colorado, the Gluten-Free Farmers Market brings together a carefully vetted lineup of gluten-free food vendors, bakeries, food trucks, artisans, wellness brands, fresh produce growers, and small businesses from across the state. Every vendor undergoes a review process focused on gluten-free safety, ingredient transparency, and cross-contact awareness to help create a market experience the gluten-free community can trust. ()

More than just a farmers market, this event is a celebration of community, accessibility, and connection. Visitors can enjoy a vibrant atmosphere filled with delicious food, handmade goods, live experiences, and opportunities to discover local businesses that truly understand the importance of safe gluten-free living. From baked goods and prepared meals to crafts, beauty products, flowers, dog treats, coffee, and specialty products, there is something for everyone to enjoy. ()

Since launching, the market has rapidly grown into a beloved community gathering, drawing thousands of attendees and supporting dozens of local gluten-free businesses throughout Colorado. Community members and vendors alike have praised the market for creating an emotional and meaningful space where people with celiac disease and gluten sensitivities can finally shop and eat with confidence. ()

Whether you are gluten-free by medical necessity, exploring a gluten-free lifestyle, supporting a loved one, or simply passionate about shopping local, the Gluten-Free Farmers Market welcomes you to experience a safer and more inclusive way to gather, shop, and connect.

For market dates, vendor information, and event updates, visit the Gluten Free Farmer’s Market website. | Season 06/13/2026–10/10/2026

Notes: Get involved in growing produce, relationships, and community! At Salida’s not-for-profit Colorado Farm to Table (CFTT) we grow approximately 10 acres of fresh produce for distribution to Coloradans in need. Starting in 2022, we are going to have a separate 1 acre plot of fresh vegetables to sell at the farmers market with all proceeds going back to our donation farm. The summer of 2022 will be our 26th season, CFTT has been welcoming people of all backgrounds in volunteer farming experiences to grow top-quality, nutritious produce for hungry families. Volunteer farm hands work with the farmer in 3-hour shifts. No experience is necessary – instruction and tools are provided. Join us! It’s a lot of fun and a great opportunity to meet and network with some awesome people. CFTT’s sustainably grown produce is distributed via partner nonprofit food pantries, soup kitchens, low-income housing, and feeding programs that redistribute the freshly harvested produce onto the plates of those most in need of nutrition relief. We encourage and welcome new volunteers, distribution partners, and innovative collaborative partnerships. Contact info@coloradofarmtotable.org for more information!

Notes: Guidestone Colorado is a Chaffee County-based, 501c3 nonprofit dedicated to growing a vibrant agricultural future through education, community building and partnerships. We serve our local community and the statewide agriculture community through our four cornerstone programs: Farm to School, Farmhands Education, Colorado Land Link, and the Hutchinson Homestead & Learning Center. The Farm to School Program fosters garden education at two school gardens and the Community & School Farm, and grows produce for Salida School District, ensuring access to local produce in school meals. Guidestone’s food production activities also include growing food for the Heart of the Rockies Regional Medical Center, supporting area CSAs and community members in growing and purchasing local food, and working with community partners on food distribution. Guidestone’s additional food system work in Chaffee County includes implementing and participating in the Chaffee Local Food Coalition, partnering with City of Salida on their Community Garden Program, and serving as a partner on several regional food system collaborations.

Notes: Growing gourmet garlic in Salida, Rocky Mountain Garlic specializes in hard neck Garlic as well as Shallots and Onions. Last season, we experimented with many different root crops and are expanding into other hardy vegetables. We are offering “shares” for purchase! Please contact us for more information and to sign up. We — Mike and Tiffany Collette — grow following organic and biodynamic processes, using an earth-friendly mentality. Our garlic is tended by hand, one clove at a time, on land that is free of chemicals. We place much importance on minimal tillage using mulches, manures, and cover crops in order to hold nutrients and rejuvenate the soil. We use drip irrigation to conserve water and bring to market a unique crop of high desert garlic. From seed to harvest to storage, our garlic is grown for you and good for you. Our mission is to provide fresh and local food, grown by people you can meet face-to-face. It is the heritage of our country and we are proud to continue the tradition!

Notes: Teller County Farmers Market Association, (TCFMA) is a 501(c)3 organization which provides a forum for sales of local produce and items associated with agriculture, gardens & food. The association, originally formed in 1990 as Woodland Park Farmers Market, is operated by volunteers and administered by a volunteer Board of Directors.  It oversees the Woodland Park Farmers' Market (Summer) and Woodland Park Holiday Market (November). MISSION: to enhance the quality of life for Teller County residents and visitors by providing access to safe and affordable produce and other food, promoting agricultural land use through a direct market for growers, encouraging organic and pesticide-free growing techniques, and fostering health and well-being through community education. The summer market has been a lively and hugely popular part of Teller County life since 1991. Products that can be found at the market include a wide variety of locally grown and produced vegetables and fruits, eggs and meats; various cheeses; locally made bread, pies & pastries, jams, honey, salsas, pickles; popcorn, lemonade, candy, high-quality locally-made crafts, and food trucks. We have Live Music each week and periodic demonstrations and educational programs. Local non-profit charitable organizations as well as other public organizations (i.e. physical and mental-health care) are well represented at our market, along with our sponsors and occasional local businesses with informational booths. | Programs: SNAP, Double Up; Season 06/05/2026–09/25/2026
